newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian border guards fire on Japanese boats.
newsitem.headline: Russian border guards fire on Japanese boats.

text.p: Russian border guards opened fire on four Japanese boats that entered Russia's territorial waters near disputed islands off northern Japan, Interfax news agency said on Thursday.

It said the Japanese vessels disregarded the border guards' warning signals and only withdrew some 25 minutes after the Russians opened fire. Earlier on Thursday, a Japanese coastguard spokesman said an unidentified ship had fired on a Japanese fishing boat, seriously injuring a crew member.

The Japanese coastguard said dense fog had cut visibility in the area at the time of the incident and added that it was not clear whether the boat involved, the Eiko-maru, was in Japanese waters or on the Russian side of the demarcation line.

Russian officials later confirmed the Interfax report. "Border guards aimed at the vessels, which then left. I cannot confirm or deny whether anybody was hurt," Pacific Ocean border guards' spokesman Sergei Kozlyov told Reuters in Vladivostok.
Moscow has repeatedly accused Japanese fishing boats of poaching in its waters around the Russian-held Southern Kurile Islands, which Tokyo claims as its Northern Territories.

The dispute over the islands has long thwarted the signing of a peace treaty between the two countries to formally end World War Two hostilities, but recently relations have improved. Last week President Boris Yeltsin said Russia would no longer point nuclear missiles at Japan.
